title: squarespace.get_order
description: Input/output contract for retrieving a single order by id. GET /orders/{id} on the commerce base URL (https://api.squarespace.com/1.0/commerce). This is a 7th action, added beyond the 5 originally scoped in connector.yaml plus list_contacts, once those six were complete. VERIFICATION STATUS: the order OBJECT SHAPE ($defs.order below) is already CONFIRMED — duplicated verbatim from create-order.schema.json/list-orders.schema.json's identical $defs.order, both live-verified 2026-08-16 against a real order (see fixtures/create-order-response.json, fixtures/orders-populated.json). What is NOT confirmed is this endpoint's own GET-by-id request/response pattern: only GET /orders (list_orders) and POST /orders (create_order) have ever been called live against this API — GET /orders/{id} has not. Unverified specifically: whether Squarespace exposes this endpoint at all, what it returns for a nonexistent id, and whether the response is wrapped in a top-level key (the way get_contact's GET-by-id turned out to be — `{ contact: {...} }`, a correction from an earlier flat placeholder model) or returned flat (the way create_order's response is, on this same commerce API). This schema models the output as FLAT (`$ref: #/$defs/order` directly, no wrapper) by analogy to create_order's confirmed flat response — but that is an assumption carried over from a sibling endpoint, not a live finding, and get_contact is direct precedent in this project for that kind of assumption turning out wrong. Needs live verification before this action can be trusted in production — see connector.yaml's known_limitations.

input.title: GetOrderInput
input.description: Retrieval is by order id, appended to the commerce base as GET /orders/{id}. Unlike the contacts base, the commerce base URL does not already end in /orders, so no segment-doubling concern exists structurally the way it did for get_contact's resolveUrl() dedup logic — but whether Squarespace's API actually serves this path at all is UNCONFIRMED; it has never been called live.

id.description: Order identifier, e.g. the `id` field on a list_orders or create_order response (real observed ids look like "6a81716f0589b404e7529648"). No format is enforced beyond non-empty.

output.title: GetOrderResult
output.description: UNCONFIRMED whether this response is wrapped in a top-level key or flat — modeled here as flat by analogy to create_order's confirmed response shape on the same commerce API. See this schema's top-level VERIFICATION STATUS.

examples.description: ILLUSTRATIVE, not a live capture through this endpoint — this endpoint has never itself been called. The order object below is the real, confirmed $defs.order shape (verbatim from create-order.schema.json's live-captured example, customerEmail replaced with a placeholder), shown here under the flat-output assumption this schema currently models. If live testing finds the real response wrapped in a key instead, this example and the output schema both need updating.
